Title: GPS to field mix of new faces, experienced leaders in Sarawak polls
Article:
KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) will field a mix of new faces and experienced leaders in the upcoming Sarawak state election.
Its chairman, Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg, said the coalition's final list of candidates would be decided at a special meeting.
Abang Johari, who is also the Sarawak Premier, said some elected representatives have chosen to step down on their own accord.
"What I can share here is that it will be a combination of the experienced and the young.
"Certainly, there will be new faces, some incumbents are not being dropped, but are instead choosing to step aside," he said in a press conference.
During the press conference, he announced the
dissolution of the assembly,
effective Oct 26, to pave the way for the 13th state election.
GPS comprises four component parties namely Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Sarawak United Peoples' Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS), and the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP).
In the Sarawak state election held on Dec 18, 2021, GPS won 76 out of the 82 contested seats.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SME Corp: Minimum wage exemption in 2027 Budget to help msmes adjust recruitment, salaries
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The RM2,000 minimum wage exemption for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with annual sales revenue below RM50 million in the 2027 Budget, effective June next year, would help businesses adjust their workforce recruitment and salary structures, said SME Corporation Malaysia.
Its chief executive officer Rizal Nainy said the exemption would give MSMEs room to align their operations with automation and digitalisation, which could improve productivity and reduce operating costs, particularly labour expenses.
"I believe that during this short-term period, as MSMEs adjust to the RM2,000 minimum wage, the government needs to introduce targeted interventions by looking at the digitalisation and automation programmes that can be made available to these businesses.
"It is also an opportunity for MSMEs to explore how automation and digitalisation can complement their workforce, ensuring that the higher wages they pay for skilled talent translate into greater value, rather than relying on low-skilled labour," he said.
Rizal said this when appearing as a guest on Bernama TV's The Nation programme, titled "Budget 2027: What It Means for MSMEs", hosted by Jessy Chahal today.
On Oct 9, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced in the 2027 Budget that the minimum wage would be raised to RM2,000 per month from RM1,700 per month, effective June 2027, benefiting more than four million workers.
He said SMEs with annual sales revenue below RM50 million would be temporarily exempted from implementing the new minimum wage of RM2,000 per month.
Additionally, Anwar said loan facilities and financing guarantees for MSMEs would be increased to RM57 billion next year from RM50 billion, while the corporate income tax rate for eligible MSMEs would be reduced by one percentage point in the 2027 Budget.
Meanwhile, Rizal said the record RM57 billion allocated for MSME financing facilities under the 2027 Budget would help businesses expand their operations, scale up and contribute more significantly to the country's gross domestic product.
"2027 is the year of MSMEs, and I believe the 2027 Budget will provide significant support for the sector.
"I hope MSMEs obtain the right information from the right sources and, more importantly, understand how to benefit from the budget to expand and scale up their businesses.
"Under the 13th Malaysia Plan, our agenda for MSMEs is about scaling up.
"We want to see micro enterprises grow into small businesses and small businesses progress into medium-sized enterprises," he added. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Doreen Choo takes Affin Pheim helm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Affin Group has appointed Doreen Choo Choy Wan as group chief executive officer of Affin Pheim Asset Management Group effective Oct 23.
Choo brings nearly three decades of experience in Malaysia's asset management industry, spanning investment management, portfolio strategy and business growth.
She will lead efforts to grow assets under management (AUM), expand market share and strengthen the group's institutional and retail businesses.
Her priorities also include widening distribution capabilities, securing strategic mandates and developing investment solutions.
Affin Pheim comprises Affin Pheim Islamic Asset Management Sdn Bhd and Affin Pheim Unit Trusts Bhd.
Affin Group president and group chief executive officer Datuk Wan Razly Abdullah said Choo's experience would support the asset manager's growth ambitions and strengthen its position in the asset and wealth management industry.
The group also aims to build a more profitable asset management business by leveraging its customer base and distribution network, in line with its Affin Axelerate 2028 Plan.
Choo holds a Bachelor of Arts in rconomics from Universiti Malaya and is a chartered financial analyst charterholder.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Allianz Life steps up agency drive
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Allianz Life Insurance Malaysia Bhd (Allianz Life) is expanding its agency network through recruitment and professional development initiatives to improve advisory capabilities and customer service.
The insurer said its 2026 Action Group Seminar & Recognition (AGSR) series brought together more than 3,000 agents and guests nationwide to recognise achievements, encourage knowledge-sharing and promote careers in life insurance.
Allianz Life chief sales officer Raymond Cheah said agents play an important role in helping customers protect their families, health and financial futures
"Through AGSR, we bring our agents together to learn, grow and celebrate their achievements, while inspiring more Malaysians to build a meaningful career where they can make a positive difference in people's lives," Cheah said in a statement.
The insurer said its "Recruit2Grow, Build to Inspire" initiative aims to attract individuals interested in entrepreneurship, personal development and leadership.
AGSR 2026 also highlighted the Allianz CEO Programme and Allianz Builder Club, which aim to develop new talent, strengthen leadership capabilities and support the long-term growth of its agency network.
The Allianz CEO Programme provides a structured pathway for high-potential individuals to become agency leaders, while both initiatives support the insurer's efforts to build a professional and customer-focused workforce.
Looking ahead to 2027, Allianz Life said it would focus on expanding its agency network, enhancing agents' capabilities and equipping them to provide protection solutions that meet Malaysians' changing needs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Perhilitan relocates 250kg male tapir from Kerteh golf club
Article:
CHUKAI: An adult male Malayan tapir that strayed into the Petronas Kerteh Golf and Recreation Club (KRGP) was captured and relocated to its forest habitat yesterday.
Terengganu Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) director Dennis Ten said four officers from the Kemaman district office carried out the operation after receiving information about the animal at 11am.
He said Perhilitan personnel began the operation at 12.30pm, using a drone to locate the tapir.
"Monitoring revealed that a tapir was in the area before the capture and relocation operation was carried out," he said in a statement.
Dennis said a physical examination found that the tapir was healthy and had sustained no injuries before it was released into the forest.
He said the animal was identified as an adult male Tapirus indicus, measuring about 160cm in length and weighing an estimated 250kg.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Waze ban: Israel data processing, legal jurisdiction among key concerns
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The government's ban on civil servants using Waze for official duties stems from cybersecurity concerns, including the processing of its data in Israel and the legal jurisdiction governing disputes involving the app.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said any dispute could only be settled in Israeli courts, posing a challenge as Malaysia does not recognise Israel and has no diplomatic relations with the country.
"Those are the two main issues," he told his weekly post-cabinet press conference today.
Fahmi said the concerns were raised by the National Cyber Security Agency with the National Security Council before being brought to the National Cyber Security Committee.
The government was also taking seriously allegations of data leaks linked to Waze, including reports that user information had been obtained by unauthorised parties and offered for sale on the dark web.
Fahmi said Waze should explain the allegations, including how personal data could have been obtained.
The Personal Data Protection Department would also be consulted on any investigation, subject to legal processes, he added.
However, he could not confirm whether the data of Malaysians was involved.
Asked whether the government would block the app, Fahmi said further action required an extract of the National Cyber Security Committee's meeting minutes.
"We are waiting for that process," he said, adding that the timing would depend on the procedures and directives involved.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Security guard claims trial to sexually assaulting 15-year-old stepsister
Article:
MELAKA: A security guard was charged at the Ayer Keroh Sessions Court today with two counts of sexual assault against his 15-year-old stepsister.
The 29-year-old accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read before judge Raja Noor Adilla Raja Mahyaldin.
According to the charges, the man was accused of committing physical sexual assault against the 15-year-old girl for sexual purposes.
The offences were allegedly committed in a room at a house in Taman Anika at 8am in mid-November 2025, and at a house in Jalan Pandan Jaya, Taman Pandan Jaya, at 3.30pm on Oct 15.
The charges were framed under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which carries a maximum prison term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Rif'ah 'Izzati Abdul Mutalif proposed bail at RM20,000 for each charge, alongside additional conditions that the accused must not intimidate the victim or prosecution witnesses and must report to the nearest police station monthly.
Lawyer Mohamed Musthafa, representing the accused, requested minimal bail, arguing that his client is single, lives with his family, and earns RM1,700 a month as a security guard.
The court allowed bail at RM10,000 with one surety for both charges, subject to the additional conditions requested by the prosecution.
The court fixed Nov 23 for document submission.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning for 11 states, three federal territories until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for several areas in 11 states and three federal territories until 6pm today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the warning covered the entire Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as all of Perlis, Terengganu and Selangor.
In Kedah, the affected areas are Bandar Baharu, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Pokok Sena, Pendang, Sik, Kuala Muda, Langkawi, Kulim and Baling.
In Perak, the warning covers Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim.
In Kelantan, the affected areas are Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang and Pasir Puteh, while in Pahang, they are Pekan, Kuantan, Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Lipis, Jerantut, Temerloh and Maran.
The warning also covers Jelebu in Negri Sembilan and the Johor districts of Kluang, Mersing, Kota Tinggi, Batu Pahat, Kulai, Johor Bahru and Pontian.
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Samarahan; Matu, Dalat and Mukah in Mukah; Sibu; Tatau and Sebauh in Bintulu; Limbang; Marudi, Telang Usan and Beleru in Miri; Maradong in Sarikei; Kuching and Bau in Kuching; and Serian.
In Sabah, the warning covers Pensiangan, Sipitang, Tenom, Kuala Penyu and Beaufort in the Interior; Tawau; Sandakan; and Ranau and Kota Belud on the West Coast.

Title: KEB sets IPO price at 35 sen, to raise RM48.49mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: KEB Bhd has set its initial public offering (IPO) price at 35 sen per share, aiming to raise RM48.49 million from its proposed listing on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia.
The property developer said the IPO involves the issuance of 138.54 million new shares.
Of the total proceeds, RM19 million will be allocated for landbank acquisition, RM14.89 million for working capital to support project development and RM8.5 million for repayment of bank borrowings.
The remaining RM6.1 million will be used for listing expenses.
Upon listing, KEB will have a market capitalisation of RM308.83 million.
Its managing director Datuk Lim Kim Chong said the prospectus launch marked a significant milestone in the company's corporate journey.
"The IPO will strengthen our financial position and provide us with additional resources to expand our landbank, support project development activities and enhance our capacity to pursue future growth opportunities," said Lim at the IPO launch today.
Since venturing into property development in 2004, KEB has completed 14 projects spanning residential, industrial, commercial and mixed-use developments.
The company currently has four ongoing developments with a combined estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM1.36 billion, alongside two future projects with an estimated GDV of RM382.73 million.
Collectively, the six projects have an estimated GDV of RM1.74 billion.
KEB also has a landbank of 24.29 hectares including land under a joint venture arrangement with landowners, to support its future development plans.
Applications for the IPO will close on Nov 2, and listing is scheduled for Nov 16.
M&A Securities Sdn Bhd is the principal adviser, sponsor, placement agent and underwriter for the IPO, while Eco Asia Capital Advisory Sdn Bhd is the financial adviser.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's offer to help Indonesia fight forest fires still stands
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia's offer to provide assets and assistance to Indonesia to combat forest fires remains open, with Jakarta yet to respond to the proposal.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the Foreign Ministry and the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry had yet to receive a response from their Indonesian counterparts.
"The prime minister expressed appreciation for the good diplomatic relations between Malaysia and Indonesia, and conveyed Malaysia's readiness to cooperate, including by providing assets to help with firefighting efforts.
"So, the offer still stands. Malaysia remains ready to provide assets if they are needed," he said at a post-cabinet press conference.
Fahmi said the cabinet had also been informed that 11 companies had been subjected to enforcement action by Indonesian authorities, as announced earlier today.
However, he said no Malaysian companies had been identified as being involved in forest burning in Indonesia.
Malaysia had previously offered to deploy a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters and 52 personnel to assist Indonesia in tackling the fires.
On Sept 19, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto
had accepted the offer
during a meeting the previous day in Hambalang, West Java.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jasmine Food expands beyond rice with coconut cream
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Jasmine Food Corporation Sdn Bhd is expanding beyond rice with the launch of Jasmine Krim Kelapa, a coconut cream product developed for food service operators and small- and medium-sized enterprises.
The product was recently launched at the Malaysia International Halal Showcase 2026 at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre.
With a 24 per cent fat content and a smooth, creamy consistency, Jasmine Krim Kelapa comes in a one-litre pack, offering convenience and consistency to businesses that regularly use coconut cream in food preparation.
The launch marks another step in Jasmine Food's evolution from a rice-focused brand into a broader food solutions provider, with products catering to Malaysian cooking and dining needs.
Jasmine Food chief operating officer Alan Kwong said the company was expanding its role from a trusted retail food brand to a food service solutions partner.
"Jasmine has always been associated with quality rice, but now we are ready to expand our role from a trusted retail food brand to a food service solutions partner.
"Jasmine Krim Kelapa is developed with businesses in mind. It is smooth, creamier, suitable for various types of cooking and, most importantly, delivers consistency in every dish."
The launch coincides with the reintroduction of two products from Jasmine Food - Jasmine Santan Kelapa in a 200ml pack and Jasmine Ketupat Mini.
While Jasmine Krim Kelapa is aimed at food service operators and businesses, the two products cater to household needs and consumers seeking convenient options for everyday cooking.
The expanded range reflects the company's strategy to diversify beyond rice while continuing to serve Malaysian households and the food service sector.
Jasmine Food said quality, value and halal assurance remained central to its product development as it expanded its portfolio.
All Jasmine products are halal-certified, reinforcing the company's commitment to providing food products for Malaysian consumers, businesses and the halal market.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MP warns against straining Petronas
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Wawasan's Machang MP Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal has warned Putrajaya against placing too great a financial burden on Petronas, saying the national oil company must retain sufficient financial strength to invest in future energy projects and safeguard Malaysia's energy security.
He said higher dividend payments to the government, uncertainty over Petronas' position in Sarawak and the company's role in securing fuel supplies during the Strait of Hormuz crisis had created a demanding set of obligations.
"Petronas has once again become the country's dependable workhorse," he said during the 2027 Budget debate in the Dewan Rakyat.
"Previously, I called it the goose that lays the golden eggs. Not everyone understood that expression. Put simply, Petronas is the company Malaysia depends on."
Wan Fayhsal said the government was relying too heavily on Petronas to support its spending plans.
"At this point, the government is squeezing Petronas to support the budget," he said.
2027 Budget projects a RM32 billion contribution from Petronas, accounting for about 8.4 per cent of the government's projected RM380.8 billion revenue next year.
This is significantly higher than the RM20 billion dividend originally provided for in Budget 2026, although the revised estimate for this year was subsequently raised to RM27 billion.
Wan Fayhsal said the issue was not whether Petronas could make the contribution, but whether it should be expected to do so without sufficient regard for its future investment requirements.
"It is not that it cannot be done. It can. But we must remember that Petronas needs to retain funds for the future," he said.
"This is especially important for oil and gas investments, which are highly capital-intensive."
Petronas' first-half results illustrate both its financial strength and the scale of its responsibilities. It recorded RM152.4 billion in revenue and RM27.2 billion in profit after tax for the six months ended June 30.
However, cash flow from operations slipped marginally to RM47.5 billion, while capital investments more than doubled year-on-year to RM41.4 billion.
These investments included upstream exploration and development, spending to sustain future production, and additional capital injected into the Pengerang Refining and Petrochemical complex.
The group declared RM20 billion in dividends to shareholders in the first half of the year.
Its cash and funds pool stood at RM193.6 billion as at June 30, down from RM204.4 billion at the end of 2025. Its net cash position was RM66.8 billion, the lowest in five years.
Wan Fayhsal said the government must consider these figures in the context of Petronas' wider national responsibilities.
"With Petronas carrying extensive subsidy-related responsibilities, what is its financial health to sustain the national budget?" he said.
He also raised the unresolved dispute over Sarawak's oil and gas regulatory framework.
"Added to this is the impasse over the gas agreement with Sarawak, where we do not yet know the final outcome," he said.
Petronas and the Sarawak government have filed separate petitions in the Federal Court concerning the validity and application of state and federal oil and gas laws. The cases are tentatively scheduled to be heard at the end of January.
The dispute is significant because more than 60 per cent of Malaysia's gas reserves are located off Borneo. Petronas has said it is seeking legal clarity on the regulatory framework governing its operations in Sarawak, while the state is challenging the continued application of several federal petroleum laws.
Wan Fayhsal said the government must also account for the costs and risks Petronas had borne in maintaining fuel supplies during the West Asia crisis.
In March, Petronas said nearly 40 per cent of Malaysia's crude oil requirements transited through the Strait of Hormuz. The company said the crisis had pushed up crude oil prices, shipping costs and insurance premiums, while domestic demand for petrol and diesel continued to exceed local supply.
Petronas said it had mobilised its integrated value chain to secure adequate supplies, supporting close to half of the domestic fuel market at the time.
"The government needs to explain to the people, in light of the challenges we face today, what is the financial health of Petronas in sustaining the national budget," Wan Fayhsal said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mobile apps face rising cyber risks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mobile application security must be built into digital platforms from the design stage, according to cybersecurity officials and industry leaders.
They said stronger threat detection, incident response and recovery measures were needed to protect essential services and public trust.
The issue took centre stage at the recent Mobile Application Resilience Forum 2026 where more than 100 industry leaders, cybersecurity professionals, technology executives and policymakers discussed growing threats to Malaysia's digital economy.
National Cyber Security Agency application and infrastructure division director Rummie Wisning, in his opening address, stressed the need for organisations to adopt a comprehensive approach to cybersecurity, backed by stronger governance and continuous security assessments.
He also highlighted the importance of public-private collaboration and alignment with Malaysia's national cybersecurity framework, including the Cyber Security Act 2024.
Zchwantech Cybersecurity Sdn Bhd chairman Datuk Seow Gim Shen said mobile application security was no longer merely an information technology concern.
It is now an economic and business imperative as digital platforms became increasingly central to interactions between businesses, government agencies and consumers.
"Cybersecurity can no longer be treated as an afterthought or merely a compliance exercise. It must be embedded into the design, development and operation of digital platforms," he said.
The forum was co-hosted by Zchwantech, Total SE Solutions Sdn Bhd, CyberSecurity Malaysia and Global CIO Forum Malaysia, with Huawei as technology partner.
Discussions also focused on CyberSecurity Malaysia's Mobile Application Certification (MAC) scheme, which independently evaluates mobile applications against defined security requirements.
Other sessions examined artificial intelligence-driven cyber threats, continuous compliance and application protection.
Zchwantech chief executive officer Wayne Wang said cooperation among government agencies, technology providers and application owners was essential to strengthen application resilience and digital trust.
He said organisations needed to shift from reactive security measures towards security-by-design as Malaysia's digital economy expands.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN candidates will not clash with BN in Melaka polls, says Takiyuddin
Article:
KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional candidates will not clash with Umno or Barisan Nasional candidates in the upcoming Melaka election, says PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan.
He said PN members had been told to support BN candidates, while BN members would also have the option of supporting PN candidates.
Takiyuddin said the cooperation between the two coalitions was initiated by Pas's central leadership and approved by the party's Syura Ulama Council.
"Our members are always obedient and loyal to the leadership. They stand with us and have confidence in this cooperation because it was initiated by Pas's central leadership and approved by the Syura Ulama Council," he said.
He said PN was fully prepared for the polls, with its election machinery from several states, including Kelantan, already mobilised despite not knowing which constituencies the coalition would contest.
"We are ready. Our machinery from various states, including Kelantan, has already gone down to the ground, even though we do not yet know which constituencies we will contest.
"However, that is not a problem. We are prepared to contest anywhere because our coalition will contest all the seats allocated to us," he said.
On candidate selection, Takiyuddin said the names would undergo the usual screening process by the coalition's leadership to ensure those chosen were suitable to represent PN.
The Melaka election is scheduled for Nov 14, with nominations on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCB targets global markets for Malaysian cocoa products
Article:
The Malaysian Cocoa Board (MCB) is expanding market access for local cocoa and chocolate products through its participation in SIAL ( Salon International de l'Alimentation) Paris 2026.
The initiative supports Malaysia's RM15.5 billion cocoa product export target for 2026.
Held from Oct 17 to 21 at Paris Nord Villepinte, France, the exhibition provided a platform for Malaysian producers to connect with international buyers, expand trade networks and boost the profile of local chocolate brands.
Marking its third participation in the event, MCB brought together six industry participants - Benns Chocolate Factory Sdn Bhd, Chocsvalley Chocolate Sdn Bhd, Francestle Chocolatier Factory Outlet (M) Sdn Bhd, Grusson Wellness Sdn Bhd, K.L. Kris Food Industries Sdn Bhd and Symphony Confection Sdn Bhd.
The participants, comprising cocoa grinders, chocolate manufacturers and entrepreneurs, showcased their products at the 54sq m MYCocoa Pavilion in Hall 5B, Booth N319.
The MCB delegation was led by Market Development and Economy Division director Theodora Sebastian.
INTEGRATED PROMOTION
The MYCocoa Pavilion featured semi-processed cocoa products, including cocoa butter and cocoa powder, alongside premium and functional Malaysian chocolates.
The range highlighted the industry's capacity to supply ingredients to food and beverage manufacturers while offering value-added products for consumer markets.
By bringing the companies together under one pavilion, MCB provided international buyers with a coordinated platform to meet Malaysian producers and explore their offerings.
The arrangement strengthened brand visibility and allowed participants to present their production and supply capabilities directly to prospective customers.
Face-to-face engagement enabled businesses to understand purchasing requirements, obtain market feedback and identify distribution opportunities.
These insights can help them assess product suitability, refine their market strategies and prioritise commercial follow-up.
BUSINESS MATCHING FOR  EXPORT OPPORTUNITIES
To boost the commercial value of its participation, MCB also organised Cocoa Business Matching sessions alongside the exhibition.
The sessions connected participating companies with international buyers to explore supply arrangements, distribution opportunities and potential trade partnerships.
The MYCocoa Pavilion also welcomed distributors and other trade visitors interested in Malaysian products and business collaboration.
Through these engagements, participants discussed market requirements and assessed opportunities for commercial partnerships, with the aim of turning initial enquiries into further negotiations and potential export orders.
Follow-up by participating companies would be essential to converting these contacts into lasting business relationships.
Connections established with buyers and distributors could open pathways into European markets and other international destinations, extending the benefits of participation beyond the exhibition.
VISIT BY AMBASSADOR AND MATRADE DELEGATION
The MYCocoa Pavilion welcomed Malaysia's ambassador to France, Datuk Eldeen Husaini Mohd Hashim, and a delegation from the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) on Oct 18.
During the visit, Theodora introduced the participating companies and chocolate entrepreneurs, highlighting their products and distinctive offerings.
The delegation also sampled Malaysian chocolate brands showcased at the pavilion.
The visit provided an opportunity for participating businesses to engage with Malaysia's diplomatic mission and Matrade, supporting efforts to explore trade opportunities, strengthen business networks and boost the international visibility of the country's cocoa industry.
ACCESS TO GLOBAL  MARKETS
Organised biennially by Comexposium, SIAL Paris (Salon International de l'Alimentation) is one of the world's leading food and beverage trade exhibitions.
The 2026 edition was expected to attract 8,000 exhibitors and 295,000 trade visitors, including importers, distributors, wholesalers, retailers and industry players.
The exhibition's international reach allowed Malaysian companies to explore multiple markets through a single platform.
Beyond meeting prospective buyers, participants also gained insights into product developments, industry trends and market requirements to inform their export strategies.
Through coordinated product promotion, business matching and engagement with international stakeholders, MCB aims to strengthen its export market development programme, improve industry competitiveness and expand distribution opportunities for Malaysian cocoa products and chocolate brands.
These efforts support the broader goal of growing Malaysia's cocoa exports and strengthening the industry's presence in international  markets.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCMC probes livestreaming of Kuching school attack
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is investigating the livestreaming of an attack on a teacher by a 16-year-old student at a private school in Kuching.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MCMC would issue a statement on the matter in due course.
"At this time, MCMC is investigating this issue.
"If we can recall, social media platforms have also failed to prevent the livestreaming of acts of violence in other countries.
"We will leave it to MCMC to investigate and make a statement in due course," he said in a post-cabinet press conference.
Fahmi was asked whether the government had sought an explanation from Meta over Facebook's failure to detect or stop the livestream when it began.
He was also asked whether Malaysia would take firmer action, including on security, to prevent violent crimes from being broadcast live.
In the incident at 8.03am on Wednesday, a female teacher sustained injuries to her hand.
Initial information indicated that the student had brought firecrackers to the school before allegedly attacking the teacher with an axe.
The student
remains hospitalised
and is under investigation.
Acting Sarawak Police Commissioner Deputy Commissioner Saifullizan Ishak said police were investigating the suspect, subject to his medical condition and the advice of medical officers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pas should have followed PN rules to avoid legal dispute, says Tun Faisal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pas should have adhered to the Perikatan Nasional constitution from the outset to prevent coalition administrative disputes from escalating to court and the Registrar of Societies (RoS).
Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz said Pas, as PN chairman and administrator, must conduct coalition affairs according to regulations and execute PN Supreme Council decisions faithfully without delay.
He said the issue would not have dragged on had non-Supreme Council Pas leaders not breached council decisions or conducted negotiations behind its back.
"Pas should not act unilaterally in violation of the PN constitution because this country has laws, and the coalition is governed by its own constitution and rules," he said in a statement today.
Commenting on yesterday's court decision, Tun Faisal said the stay order did not determine whether the RoS decision was wrong, nor did it prove that Pas had not violated the coalition constitution or oppressed Bersatu.
Yesterday, the High Court granted a stay on the RoS notice, allowing PN to proceed with its Melaka election preparations using its name and logo.
The decision by Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad enables PN to continue political activities pending the disposal of its judicial review, clearing the path ahead of nomination day on Oct 31 and polling on Nov 14.
Previously, PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan reportedly said the coalition would hold a meeting soon following the High Court ruling.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three Melaka excos tipped to be dropped in BN candidate shake-Up
Article:
MELAKA: At least three state executive councillors are expected to be dropped from Barisan Nasional's (BN) line-up for the Nov 14 state election, with several new faces tipped to contest as the coalition prepares to announce its candidates tomorrow.
Those believed to be at risk are state Youth, Sports and NGO Development Committee chairman Datuk VP Shanmugam, who is also Melaka MIC chairman; Women, Family and Community Development Committee chairman Datuk Kalsom Nordin, who heads the state Umno Wanita wing; and Education, Higher Education and Religious Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Rahmad Mariman.
Shanmugam is the incumbent for Gadek, Kalsom for Pengkalan Batu and Rahmad for Ayer Molek.
Other incumbents said to be facing possible exclusion include former chief minister Datuk Seri Sulaiman Md Ali (Lendu), Datuk Zaidi Attan (Serkam) and Datuk Siti Faizah Abd Aziz (Sungai Rambai).
Among the new faces tipped for candidacy is Melaka Umno Youth chief and chief minister's political secretary Datuk Abdul Hakim Abdul Wahid, who is expected to contest outside his Masjid Tanah division.
Serkam is among the seats linked to him, reportedly due to his extensive family ties in the constituency.
Melaka Umno Puteri chief Nurul Amirah Mohd Yusof is also tipped to contest in Lendu should Sulaiman be dropped.
Other names in the running include Hang Tuah Jaya Umno division chief Datuk Mohd Ridhwan Mohd Ali, who is linked to Ayer Molek, and Jasin Umno deputy division chief Datuk Azman Abdullah, who is tipped for Sungai Rambai.
Also mentioned are Jasin Umno Puteri chief Asmah Sulaiman, Jasin Umno division committee member Hairul Amin Madon, Kota Melaka Umno division secretary Datuk Akramuddin Abd Aziz and Masjid Tanah Umno division secretary Mohd Hafith Alias.
The potential reshuffle points to a significant revamp of BN's candidate line-up, with party wing leaders and division officials possibly given the opportunity to replace incumbents. However, the final list remains subject to the party leadership's decision.
BN will contest 21 of the 28 state seats, with the remaining seven allocated to Pas and its political allies under a seat-sharing agreement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bersatu remains PN member despite meeting dispute, says PAS deputy president
Article:
KOTA BARU: Bersatu remains a component party of Perikatan Nasional and retains the right to be invited to coalition meetings, Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said.
He said Bersatu was previously invited to meetings, but this ceased after the party lodged a complaint with the Registrar of Societies (RoS).
"Bersatu is still a PN member, so as a member, it has rights. We actually invited them previously, but stopped because of their complaint to the RoS.
"When there is a complaint, we are in a dilemma. If the complaint holds, any meeting would be invalid, and if we invite them, we would also be affected.
"To prevent this, we wrote to the Bersatu secretary-general seeking clarification on their status, as they claimed the meeting lacked a quorum, but the letter was never answered," he told a press conference here today.
Yesterday, PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan reportedly said PN intends to invite Bersatu to attend coalition meetings in the near future, following a High Court decision granting a stay on the RoS action against PN pending judicial review.
Takiyuddin said PN will hold a meeting soon following the court ruling.
The dispute arose after the party led by Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin lodged a complaint with the RoS, alleging it was excluded from a PN Supreme Council meeting on July 16 and questioning its membership status.
The RoS confirmed receiving the complaint on Aug 11 before issuing a show-cause notice to PN on Sept 22, asking the coalition to explain why its registration should not be revoked.
A day later, the RoS suspended PN's activities under Subsection 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966 before deregistering the coalition on Oct 20 under Subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of the same act.
Tuan Ibrahim explained that as a precaution, it was best not to invite Bersatu, while maintaining that the party remains part of PN.
He added that Bersatu had indicated a desire to part ways based on several announcements ahead of the Melaka election.
"Bersatu declared that in the Melaka election, it wants to contest independently, use its own logo, and even form a new alliance as it did in Negri Sembilan.
"So we interpret these statements as an indication that they no longer wish to remain with PN," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED]: Govt wants detailed explanation from MHA, Prosignal over Tuju app issues
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The government has directed the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA) and Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd to explain technical issues reported by users of the TuJu navigation application.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the explanation must cover the root causes of the problems, technical aspects, current performance, and ongoing or planned corrective measures.
"MHA has acknowledged that users are facing problems and has informed us that efforts to improve the application are under way," he said in a post-cabinet press conference.
Fahmi said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar was coordinating a meeting involving the secretaries-general of several ministries.
The meeting would review the use of navigation applications, including locally developed alternatives, and ensure that Waze was no longer used, particularly by civil servants.
"The meeting will also examine MHA and Prosignal Consortium's explanations.
"This includes the technical aspects, functional effectiveness, user experience and an improvement action plan with clear targets and timelines."
Tuju went
offline yesterday
for system upgrades, temporarily disrupting its navigation function just a day after the government encouraged Malaysians to switch from Waze to the locally developed alternative.
The move comes after the government banned civil servants from using Waze while on official duty, citing concerns over data security and the application's links to Israel.
The directive, which took immediate effect, followed a decision made at the
National Cyber Security Committee meeting
chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Oct 20.
Shamsul Azri later
instructed ministry secretaries-general
and department heads to ensure the directive was communicated to civil servants under their supervision.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN-Pas seat deal gives strategic edge in Melaka polls – analyst
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional's decision to contest 21 seats in the Melaka election, while Pas and its allies contest seven, gives the two sides a strategic advantage by reducing the risk of clashes and vote splitting.
Political analyst Mujibu Abd Muis said the seat allocation would allow both sides to focus their machinery and resources on their respective constituencies, although it did not guarantee victory as voter support could not be transferred automatically between parties.
"The advantage of this formula is that BN and Pas can retain their respective identities and strengths, with BN drawing on its administrative experience while Pas mobilises its traditional support base.
"The use of the BN logo shows that the cooperation does not require the two parties to abandon their political identities. However, its effectiveness depends on the suitability of candidates and the realities of local support," he said when contacted.
Mujibu said an effective seat allocation should take into account previous election results, voter demographics, local networks and the capabilities of each party's machinery, rather than merely an agreement reached at leadership level.
He said the arrangement would force Pakatan Harapan to brace for a more coordinated challenge, although it could still compete by fielding strong candidates, addressing economic concerns and offering a convincing alternative.
"The main strength of the (BN-Pas) cooperation lies in the combined organisational resources and grassroots networks. However, the biggest risk is assuming that support for the leaders will automatically translate into support from their respective grassroots members," he said.
Mujibu identified three key risks: incomplete vote transfers between supporters of the two parties, dissatisfaction among party machinery and conflicting political identities and messaging.
"If dissatisfaction arises because a party is forced to give up a stronghold, it could lead to quiet sabotage, half-hearted campaigning or weaker voter mobilisation," he said.
On voter sentiment in Melaka, Mujibu said public acceptance could not be assessed solely through racial demographics, as government performance, candidates' credibility and household economic concerns would also influence voting decisions.
Among Malay voters, he said, the cooperation could be seen as an effort to consolidate political strength. However, the narrative of Malay unity would only be effective if supported by clear policy proposals rather than slogans.
"Non-Malay voters will assess BN's position in the cooperation and whether there are assurances that the interests of all communities will continue to be protected without being undermined by particular political approaches," he said.
On young voters, Mujibu said they tended to be more open-minded and less bound by traditional party loyalties, with greater emphasis on issues such as employment opportunities, wages and housing costs.
He said BN and Pas could benefit from coordinating support among certain voter groups, while PH's advantage would depend on its ability to build public confidence through consistent and inclusive messaging.
"Voter acceptance will not be determined solely by the identity of the coalition, but by the extent to which the cooperation is seen as capable of bringing tangible benefits to their lives," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Corporate mafia task force terms of reference to be tabled next week
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The terms of reference for a special task force investigating alleged corporate mafia activities will be tabled at next week's cabinet meeting.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim informed the cabinet of the matter at today's meeting.
"The prime minister also announced that the findings would be made public within three months of the investigation being completed, as stated in Parliament during Prime Minister's Question Time last Tuesday," he said at a press conference.
Anwar had told the Dewan Rakyat that a
special task force
led by the Attorney-General had been formed to coordinate investigations involving all relevant enforcement agencies.
He said Bukit Aman's anti-money laundering crime investigation team had
frozen
RM4.3 billion and seized RM1 billion in a series of investigations into alleged corporate mafia activities between late 2022 and September this year.
The team had also forfeited RM48.3 million and imposed compounds totalling RM1.1 billion in connection with the cases during the period.
The allegations came to prominence following a Bloomberg report in February accusing the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) of allegedly helping a group of businessmen take control of publicly listed companies.
MACC chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki and the commission have denied the allegations.
Bloomberg also reported that Azam held 17.7 million shares in Velocity Capital, citing a filing with the Companies Commission of Malaysia. The shareholding was
disclosed
in the company's annual return and was valued at about RM800,000 based on its share price.
Azam has maintained that his stake in the financial services company was declared and above board.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak assembly to dissolve next Monday, state polls within 60 days [WATCH]
Article:
KUCHING: The Sarawak state assembly will be dissolved on Oct 26 to pave the way for the state's 13th election.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg announced the dissolution today after obtaining the consent of Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar.
Abang Johari said the 19th Sarawak assembly first convened on Feb 14, 2022, under Article 21(3) of the Sarawak State Constitution.
He said since securing the people's mandate in the Dec 18, 2021 state election, the Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) government had worked to advance the state's development.
This includes strengthening the economy, improving infrastructure and public services, and safeguarding Sarawak's rights and interests in accordance with the Federal Constitution and the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
"The GPS government has achieved various milestones, which I outlined in my winding-up speech at the recently concluded state assembly sitting.
"These achievements reflect the GPS government's efforts to improve the people's well-being and build a better future for Sarawak," he said.
Abang Johari said as the assembly's term approached its end, it was appropriate to seek a fresh mandate from the people to allow them to choose their government through the democratic process.
"In line with the practice of parliamentary democracy, and to safeguard the people's right to choose their government democratically, Sarawakians must be given the opportunity to elect a new government with a fresh mandate to continue the state's development agenda.
"Accordingly, the Yang di-Pertua Negeri has consented to my request to dissolve the assembly. Under Article 21(2) of the Sarawak State Constitution, the assembly will be dissolved effective Oct 26," he said.
Under Article 21(4) of the state constitution, the election must be held within 60 days of the dissolution, while the new assembly must convene no later than 120 days from that date.
He said the Election Commission would be formally notified of the dissolution to allow preparations for the election.
During the interim period, he said, the state government would function as a caretaker government in accordance with constitutional requirements and conventions, while ensuring that public administration and essential services continued to operate for the people's welfare.
Abang Johari also thanked Sarawakians for their trust and support throughout the assembly's term, and expressed appreciation to assemblymen and civil servants for carrying out their responsibilities.
He urged all parties, candidates and supporters, to respect the law and conduct themselves responsibly throughout the election period.
The Sarawak assembly currently has 82 seats and is set to expand to 99 following the EC's approval of 17 additional constituencies.
In the previous election, GPS won 76 of the 82 seats, while Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) won four and DAP secured two.
The four seats won by PSB were Bawang Assan, Engkilili, Ba'Kelalan and Batu Lintang.
