Title: Anwar expects Israeli opposition following Waze ban
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim believes Israel will use its influence against Malaysia following the government's decision to ban civil servants from using the Waze navigation application.
He said Malaysia's firm opposition to Israel meant the government's actions were likely to be closely monitored, but stressed that national security remained the priority.
"Malaysia is among the countries that strongly oppose the cruel Zionist Israeli regime.
"Naturally, our actions are being monitored.
"I believe that after this, they will use all their influence to oppose us.
"But that is all right. The people must understand," he told reporters after attending Friday prayers at Masjid Al-Mustaqim in Taman Nirwana, Ampang, today.
On Wednesday, the government announced a ban on Waze among civil servants, citing concerns over the potential misuse of government information and users' personal data by the Israeli regime.
In a statement, the Prime Minister's Office said the decision took into account Waze Mobile Ltd's status as a data controller incorporated and operating under Israeli law.
The government said the move was intended to prevent potential threats to national security and protect sensitive information.
Waze has denied allegations that it collects sensitive government information or allows third parties to exploit users' personal data.
The company described the allegations as untrue and maintained that it operates under strict privacy policies and complies with applicable data protection standards.
Waze was developed in Israel in 2008 and acquired by American technology company Google in 2013.
Its navigation service uses GPS information and reports submitted by motorists to provide real-time traffic updates, route suggestions and alerts about road hazards.
Although Waze is owned by Google, its operating company, Waze Mobile Ltd, is incorporated in Israel, and its terms of use specify Israeli law as the governing jurisdiction.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo clarified in Parliament yesterday that the restriction applied to civil servants carrying out official duties and did not extend to the general public.
The government has also encouraged the use of locally developed navigation applications, including TuJu, as alternatives to Waze.
However, TuJu has faced complaints over technical shortcomings, prompting LLM to announce system improvements affecting its navigation function.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IGP warns declining respect for senior officers could weaken police force
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail has reminded police personnel to maintain discipline and respect senior officers to preserve the force's strength and harmony.
Khalid said respect for senior officers appeared to be declining, raising concerns that this could weaken the force and undermine its standing among other government agencies.
"We know that observing the proper chain of command is essential. We must show respect to the seniors," he said at the IGP's monthly gathering organised by the Integrity and Standards Compliance Department at Bukit Aman today.
He reminded personnel to maintain the discipline instilled during training throughout their service, adding that being reprimanded should not be viewed negatively, but taken as an opportunity to improve.
"Being corrected is not a wrongdoing in itself, but should serve as a lesson to help personnel recognise that a mistake has been made.
"We should not view being reprimanded as a sign of weakness. We should ensure criticisms are constructive and help build character, enabling us to fulfil our duties and responsibilities with greater competence, discipline, and integrity," he said.
Khalid said personnel must respect one another, accept feedback, and acknowledge that they are not always right, while fostering cooperation and solidarity within the force.
Meanwhile, he said the police will celebrate Integrity Day on Nov 11 under the theme "Integriti dan Organisasi Bukan Pilihan Tetapi Kewajipan" (Integrity and Organisation: Not a Choice, but an Obligation).
He added that the celebration will honour 35 police personnel who rejected bribes in the line of duty, recognising them as role models for their colleagues.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Poorest households left with just 1.8pct income buffer: KRI
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's poorest households are left with just 1.8 per cent of gross income after consumption expenses in 2024, down sharply from 10.8 per cent in 2019, as rising spending eroded their financial buffers.
Median monthly household expenditure reached RM4,758 in 2024, growing at an annualised rate of 5.3 per cent from 2022 compared with 5.1 per cent annual growth in median household income to RM7,017, according to Khazanah Research Institute (KRI).
KRI, in its "From Income to Wellbeing: The State of Households 2026" report, said expenditure among the bottom 10 per cent of households by income rose 21.3 per cent between 2019 and 2024.
Across the bottom 70 per cent of households, spending increased by more than 15 per cent over the same period, while expenditure among the top 10 per cent barely changed.
The shrinking financial buffer leaves poorer households with less capacity to absorb further increases in living costs or build savings.
KRI noted that the residual income measure excludes other outgoings, including taxes, loan repayments and transfers to other households, which would further reduce the amount available for savings.
Health and lifestyle trends also add to household pressures. Malaysian households spent an average of RM902.70 a month eating out in 2024, exceeding the RM875.80 spent on food at home.
Meanwhile, 54.4 per cent of Malaysian adults were overweight or obese in 2023, while physical activity declined between 2019 and 2023, the report found.
KRI said household wellbeing must be assessed beyond income and expenditure, taking into account health and other factors that affect living standards.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar apologises for Waze ban inconvenience, says national security comes first
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has apologised for any inconvenience caused by the government's ban on Waze among civil servants, but maintained that national security must take precedence over convenience.
He acknowledged that the decision had drawn criticism, with some questioning why the government had acted so quickly.
However, Anwar said the risks identified by the government were serious enough to warrant immediate action.
"I know I have been criticised and condemned for being hasty.
"If this causes some inconvenience, I apologise. But to me, national security is more important," he told reporters after attending Friday prayers at Masjid Al-Mustaqim in Taman Nirwana, Ampang, today.
He said he had ordered checks into Waze's operations and legal arrangements, which he said confirmed that the navigation application was linked to Israel and that its terms were governed by Israeli law.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said he understood complaints about the
limitations
of locally developed navigation applications, including TuJu.
He maintained that the inconvenience was a price worth paying to protect sensitive information.
"It is better to be safe than to hand over confidential state information, your personal information and the country's information to Israel.
"That is what matters to us," he said.
He also urged Malaysians to understand the government's position, particularly given Malaysia's strong opposition to Israel.
Anwar said the government would continue examining alternative navigation applications while improvements were made to existing local options.
On Wednesday, the government announced a ban on the use of Waze among civil servants, citing concerns over the potential misuse of government information and users' personal data by the Israeli regime.
In a statement, the Prime Minister's Office said the decision took into account Waze Mobile Ltd's
status
as a data controller incorporated and operating under Israeli law.
The government said the move was necessary to prevent potential threats to national security and protect sensitive information.
Waze has denied allegations that it collects sensitive government information or allows third parties to exploit users' personal data.
The company described the allegations as untrue and maintained that it operates under strict privacy policies and complies with applicable data protection standards.
The government has also encouraged the use of locally developed navigation applications, including TuJu, developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA).
However, TuJu has faced complaints over technical shortcomings, prompting the MHA to announce improvements to its navigation function.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysians' wellbeing improves, but income gaps persist: Khazanah research arm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's household wellbeing has improved across several measures, but sharp regional income disparities and uneven access to higher-paying jobs continue to shape living standards, Khazanah Research Institute (KRI) said.
Median monthly household income reached RM7,017 in 2024, rising at an annual rate of 5.1 per cent from 2022, while the labour force participation rate increased to 70.6 per cent from 69.3 per cent in 2022 and 68.7 per cent in 2019.
The Malaysia Happiness Index also rose to 7.60 in 2024 from 6.48 in 2021, said KRi in its "From Income to Wellbeing: The State of Households 2026" report today.
The Malaysian Wellbeing Index showed that economic and social wellbeing had generally improved since 2000.
However, the gains remain uneven geographically, with economic activity and higher-paying jobs concentrated in urban centres, particularly Selangor and Kuala Lumpur, according to KRI.
In 2024, median monthly wages stood at RM2,851 in urban areas, against RM1,698 in rural areas. Rural median household income was just 56.4 per cent of the urban level.
Of Malaysia's 166 districts, 111 recorded poverty rates above the national rate of 5.1 per cent in 2024, highlighting persistent disparities in economic opportunities.
Access to basic services has improved considerably. In 2024, 97.8 per cent of households were within 5km of a public health facility, while 98.7 per cent were within 5km of a primary school and 95.9 per cent within 5km of a secondary school.
Nearly all households also had access to treated piped water, electricity and telecommunications.
KRI cautioned that higher incomes and access to infrastructure alone do not guarantee better wellbeing. Age, gender and employment conditions also matter.
Older households tend to have lower incomes and greater health risks, while women continue to face lower labour force participation and a persistent wage gap.
Informal workers, particularly in rural areas, also face greater job insecurity and weaker access to employment-related protections.
The report further warned that Malaysia's dependence on a limited number of countries for food imports exposes households to potential supply disruptions and price shocks.
Such increases would weigh more heavily on lower-income households, which spend a larger share of their budgets on food.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hold, hike and cut? Bank Indonesia says there's logic to the policy mix
Article:
JAKARTA: Bank Indonesia (BI) on Friday pushed back against criticism by some in the market that its latest policy package was confusing, saying the measures were aimed at improving how its decisions flow through to the broader economy.
The central bank this week kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged, raised the overnight deposit facility rate, announced cuts to banks' reserve requirement ratio (RRR) and offered more foreign exchange hedging discounts, in a policy mix that some economists described as "perplexing", "confusing" or "complex".
"This is BI's strategy to harmonise and synchronise our policy rate with our monetary operations strategy," Firman Mochtar, BI's head of economic and monetary policy, told a press conference.
Firman said the higher deposit facility rate restored a symmetrical interest-rate corridor, bringing both the deposit and lending facility rates to 75 basis points from the benchmark rate.
BI had previously maintained a wider 100-basis-point gap between the benchmark and deposit rates because of government fund placements in commercial banks, he said.
He was referring to the government's controversial decision to move excess cash from BI to state-controlled banks to increase banking liquidity. Following a change in leadership at the finance ministry, some of the funds have been withdrawn.
Going forward, it would be better to harmonise the policy rate corridor with BI's monetary targets, Firman said.
He added that the corridor adjustment was consistent with the central bank's planned reserve-requirement cuts.
BI has briefed market participants on the changes, he said.
The central bank plans to cut reserve requirements by a cumulative 200 basis points by December. However, changes to its liquidity incentive scheme mean the effective reserve ratio will fall to about two per cent, roughly 100 basis points below its previous level.
"The additional liquidity is not massive. We have calculated and it's consistent with the BI rate and economic activities," Firman said, estimating an increase of 90 trillion rupiah (US$4.98 billion) in liquidity.
Erwin Gunawan Hutapea, BI's head of monetary management, said the central bank also wants banks to favour shorter-dated instruments over parking excess funds in its rupiah securities, known as SRBI.
BI had previously raised interest rates on SRBI to attract foreign capital inflows. However, Erwin said BI has reduced the level of outstanding SRBI from 1,096 trillion rupiah in July to below 950 trillion rupiah now.
Bank of America economists initially labelled BI's policy mix as "hold, hike and cut all at once" and "perplexing". They later said in a note the measures were less contradictory than they first appeared.
"The RRR cuts do not necessarily signal a reduced willingness to hike policy rate if needed, in our view," they wrote.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Comfort Gloves agrees to settle RM99.3mil IRB tax dispute for RM8.3mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Comfort Gloves Bhd has reached an agreement with the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) to settle a two-year tax dispute involving its subsidiaries for RM8.3 million, a fraction of the original amount.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the glove manufacturer said its subsidiaries, Comfort Rubber Gloves Industries Sdn Bhd (CRGI) and Gallant Quality Sdn Bhd (GQ), reached the agreement on Oct 22, subject to the finalisation of settlement documentation.
"The settlement is not expected to have any material financial impact on the group, as the settlement amount has been provided for in CRGI and GQ's financial statements," it said.
Upon finalisation of the documentation, the subsidiaries will discontinue all legal proceedings over the disputed tax assessments, bringing the matter to a full and final resolution.
The dispute began in April 2024 when both subsidiaries initiated legal proceedings against the IRB over additional tax assessments totalling RM99.3 million.
The assessments arose from the IRB's reassessment of the tax basis period following Comfort Gloves' change of financial year-end to Dec 31, 2021, despite the company having previously obtained the necessary approval.
At 2.40pm, Comfort Gloves' shares were up half a sen, or 3.03 per cent, at 17 sen, valuing the company at RM99.1 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RoS challenges court stay on Perikatan deregistration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS) has filed an appeal against the High Court’s decision allowing Perikatan Nasional (PN) to suspend action by RoS to deregister the political coalition.
According to documents obtained by the media, Federal Counsel representing RoS director-general Datuk Mohd Zulfikar Ahmad and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail filed the notice of appeal at the Court of Appeal today, following their dissatisfaction with the decision delivered by High Court Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad yesterday.
Judge Azizan also allowed PN’s application to stay the implementation of RoS’ notice suspending all activities of the political coalition pending the court’s decision on its application for judicial review.
The decision paves the way for PN to contest the Melaka state election, scheduled for Nov 14.
Meanwhile, lawyer Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, representing the coalition, confirmed the filing of the notice of appeal.
On Oct 13, the court dismissed PN’s application for an interim stay of the RoS suspension notice but granted the political coalition leave to initiate judicial review proceedings.
The judicial review application was filed on Oct 5 by PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, together with Parti Gerakan Rakyat Malaysia (Gerakan) secretary-general Wong Chia Zhen, Malaysian Indian People Party (MIPP) secretary-general N. Sathes Kumar, Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah and Parti Pejuang Tanahair (Pejuang) secretary-general Datuk Sazmi Miah, named as the first to fifth applicants respectively.
RoS had earlier issued an order suspending all PN activities with effect from Sept 23. According to an RoS statement, the action was taken under Subsection 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966, following a notice issued to PN on Sept 22.
In their application, the applicants claimed that the suspension prevented them from carrying out their political activities as usual, including using the coalition’s name and symbol to contest the 16th Melaka state election.
Among other things, the applicants sought a certiorari order to quash the suspension order and the notice proposing PN’s deregistration.
On Oct 20, RoS deregistered PN under subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of the Societies Act 1966 after finding that the coalition’s explanation had failed to rebut the grounds for deregistration set out in the notice dated Sept 22. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Perikatan seat talks with Umno to be finalised within days, says Tuan Ibrahim
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 23 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) is still negotiating to finalise seat allocations for the Melaka state election, with the coalition seeking one or two more seats on top of the seven discussed with Umno so far.
PN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said talks were ongoing, and a final decision, including on any additional seats, was expected soon.
He said the discussions were now at the main committee level and would be finalised at a meeting expected within the next day or two.
“So far it is not final. Although the seven seats mentioned by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi are seats not won by Barisan Nasional (BN), we are still negotiating for one or two more seats.
“We expect it could be finalised today or tomorrow, God willing,” he told a press conference here today, Sinar Harian reported.
He was speaking after delivering a talk at the Kuliah Pagi Jumaat Perdana, held in conjunction with the Karnival Rakyat 36 Tahun Membangun Bersama Islam at Dataran Warisan, Stadium Sultan Muhammad IV.
Tuan Ibrahim said Umno had so far regarded the seven seats as those to be retained under the arrangement, but PAS hoped further talks would open the way for additional seats.
He said the final decision on seat allocation would be made by the parties’ top leadership through the seat negotiation committee.
On the seven seats under discussion, he said they comprised four seats won by DAP and three Malay-majority constituencies.

Title: Malaysia keeps Indonesia firefighting aid offer open, no local companies linked to forest fires
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — Malaysia’s offer to help Indonesia tackle forest fires causing transboundary haze remains open, with the government ready to provide firefighting assets if needed, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
He said the Foreign Ministry and the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES) had yet to receive a full response from Indonesia on the type of assistance it was prepared to accept.
“The offer still stands. Malaysia remains ready to provide assistance and assets if required,” he told his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.
Fahmi said the Prime Minister had expressed appreciation for the strong diplomatic ties between Malaysia and Indonesia and reaffirmed Malaysia’s willingness to assist in efforts to put out the fires.
He said the Cabinet had also been briefed on the haze situation by the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister.
Fahmi added that the Cabinet had been informed of an announcement by Indonesian authorities this morning that 11 companies had been subjected to action over the issue.
However, no Malaysian companies had so far been identified as being involved in forest-burning activities in Indonesia, he said.
The haze affecting Malaysia has been linked to smoke drifting across national borders from fires in neighbouring Indonesia, raising concerns over air quality, particularly in parts of the Klang Valley.

Title: Plan your commute: Severe weather warning for KL, Selangor, and nine other states this evening
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for several areas in 11 states and three federal territories until 6 pm today.
In a statement today, MetMalaysia said the adverse weather conditions in Peninsular Malaysia would affect the entire Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as the whole of Perlis, Terengganu and Selangor.
In Kedah, the affected areas are Bandar Baharu, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Pokok Sena, Pendang, Sik, Kuala Muda, Langkawi, Kulim and Baling, while in Perak, they are Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim.
In Kelantan, the warning covers Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang and Pasir Puteh, while in Pahang, it covers Pekan, Kuantan, Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Lipis, Jerantut, Temerloh and Maran.
The same warning has also been issued for Jelebu in Negeri Sembilan, and the Johor districts of Kluang, Mersing, Kota Tinggi, Batu Pahat, Kulai, Johor Bahru and Pontian.
In Sarawak, the weather conditions are expected to affect Samarahan, Mukah (Matu, Dalat and Mukah), Sibu, Bintulu (Tatau and Sebauh), Limbang, Miri (Marudi, Telang Usan and Beleru), Sarikei (Maradong), Kuching (Kuching and Bau) and Serian.
In Sabah, the warning covers the Interior (Pensiangan, Sipitang, Tenom, Kuala Penyu and Beaufort), Tawau, Sandakan and the West Coast (Ranau and Kota Belud). — Bernama

Title: Corporate mafia task force’s terms of reference to go before Cabinet next week, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — The terms of reference for a special task force investigating allegations of a “corporate mafia” will be presented to the Cabinet next week, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
He said the task force’s findings would be made public within three months of the completion of the investigation, in line with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement in Parliament earlier this week.
“The Prime Minister also informed the Cabinet that the terms of reference for the special task force that will investigate the findings related to the corporate mafia issue will be presented at next week’s Cabinet meeting,” Fahmi said at his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.
Anwar said in Parliament on Tuesday that he had instructed a special task force led by the Attorney General to finalise its investigation and publicly disclose its findings within three months.
The investigation follows allegations of a purported “corporate mafia” reported by Bloomberg, which cited dozens of unnamed sources, including individuals purported to be serving Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and police officers.
The reports alleged that a group had plotted hostile takeovers of companies linked to projects awarded through government tenders.

Title: UK-based Malaysian lawyer named Multilaw chair-elect
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Malaysian lawyer Joanne Vengadesan has made history after being elected chair of Multilaw, a global network of law firms spanning over 100 countries with 300 offices.
The United Kingdom-based practitioner, who has 25 years of legal experience, was elected at Multilaw’s Global Conference in Prague earlier this month. She will serve a two-year term starting in September 2027, succeeding Australian lawyer Paul Kirton.
She began her career when she was called to the Malaysian Bar as an Advocate and Solicitor in 1997, initially practising intellectual property law in Kuala Lumpur.
Currently a partner at leading international firm Penningtons Manches Cooper LLP, Joanne is the daughter of retired Malaysian diplomat Datuk R. Vengadesan, who served as the country’s ambassador to several nations, including Italy and Namibia.
In a statement, Joanne said it was an honour to be named chair-elect, and she looks forward to taking on the role of chair next year.
“I love the perspective that being a Malaysian and working in the UK gives me. Malaysia is so multicultural that we grow up being so comfortable and at home with all our communities and cultures,” she said.
Joanne said her international upbringing played a significant role in fostering her interest in being part of a global legal community such as Multilaw. Her legal practice in the UK regularly handled cross-border matters.
“Multilaw has played a huge role in my career, and I am excited about the new challenges and opportunities to come. I could not be more proud of this network, which continues to go from strength to strength.
“The depth of the relationships and layers of connections between Multilaw member firms enable us to leverage the significant trust between us for the benefit of our respective clients. I am also very proud of my firm, Penningtons Manches Cooper’s, continued commitment and active engagement across the network,” she said.
Meanwhile, Penningtons Manches Cooper LLP chief executive officer Helen Drayton said she was pleased and proud of Joanne’s appointment, describing it as a testament to her talent, dedication and close collaboration with colleagues across the firm and the Multilaw network.
Multilaw chief executive officer Adam Cooke, who has known Joanne for nearly 20 years, said he had witnessed first-hand her energy, insight and warmth, adding that she understood the network’s emphasis on strong relationships, mutual trust and shared ambitions for its member firms and their clients. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi says Malaysians can use any navigation app except Waze, including overseas alternatives
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — Malaysians are free to use any navigation application other than Waze, including alternatives developed locally or overseas, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
He said the government was not directing the public towards a single alternative amid concerns over Waze’s data security and ongoing efforts to improve the locally developed TuJu application.
“The government encourages the use of various applications. There are various alternatives, both locally developed and those from overseas.
“What is important is that Waze is not used, due to security concerns that have been communicated by the National Security Council,” he said at his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.
“We are not directing everyone towards a single application. People can use various alternative navigation applications other than Waze,” he added.
Fahmi said the concerns over Waze were based on feedback from the National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa), which was conveyed to the National Security Council (MKN) and subsequently discussed by the National Cyber Security Committee (JKSN).
He said two key issues had been raised: the transfer of data collected and processed through the application to Israel, and the fact that any legal disputes would have to be handled through Israeli courts.
“Any legal disputes would be handled exclusively through the courts in Israel. This means that if any issues arise, we would not be able to pursue them there because Malaysia does not recognise Israel and has no diplomatic relations with it,” he said.
On TuJu, Fahmi said the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) had acknowledged the problems reported by users and was working to improve the application.
However, he said LLM and its developer, ProSignal Konsortium Sdn Bhd, needed to provide detailed explanations of the technical problems, the application’s current performance and the measures being taken to address users’ complaints.
He said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar had been asked to coordinate a meeting involving the secretaries-general of several ministries to examine the use of navigation applications, including local alternatives, and ensure Waze was no longer used, particularly by civil servants.
The meeting would also examine explanations from LLM and ProSignal Konsortium, as well as TuJu’s functionality, user experience and improvement plans, including clear targets and timelines.
The ban on Waze was decided at a JKSN meeting, with Shamsul Azri instructing department heads to ensure it was implemented immediately.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said on Tuesday that the government was looking into security risks arising from Waze, which he said was subject to Israeli laws.
Nacsa later clarified that the ban applied only to civil servants on official duty, although it encouraged them to uninstall Waze and switch to a local alternative.
LLM had apologised for disruptions to TuJu, attributing them to a surge in new users after Anwar’s call, while users also complained about its navigation and route accuracy.
Waze has rejected claims that it collects sensitive government information or allows any party to exploit users’ personal data, calling them false.

Title: BDS Malaysia backs civil service Waze ban, urges public boycott of navigation app
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — BDS Malaysia has welcomed the government’s directive banning civil servants from using Waze and its call for members of the public to stop using the navigation application.
In a statement today, the organisation said it supported the directive, citing concerns that the use of Waze could compromise Malaysia’s national security and sovereignty.
“We fully support this directive which is issued in the interest of preventing our national security and sovereignty from being compromised by Waze, an Israeli-based company, for the benefit of the Zionist apartheid and genocidal regime,” the statement read.
BDS Malaysia also urged the government to remain consistent in addressing national security concerns.
BDS Malaysia is part of the global Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) movement, which campaigns for boycotts, divestment and sanctions against Israel in support of Palestinian rights.
On Wednesday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim ordered civil servants to stop using Waze over concerns that sensitive government information and personal data could be exploited by Israel. — Bernama

Title: Architect charged with molesting senior cop’s son at Melawati gym sauna
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — An architect pleaded not guilty in the Ampang Magistrate’s Court today to a charge of molesting the son of a senior police officer at a gymnasium in Taman Melawati last Sunday.
Datuk Saiful Anuar Abdul Aziz, 61, is accused of using criminal force against the 18-year-old victim with intent to outrage his modesty in a sauna room at a gymnasium in a shopping mall in Taman Melawati at 7.10 pm on Oct 18.
The charge, framed under Section 354 of the Penal Code, carries a maximum penalty of 10 years’ imprisonment, a fine or whipping, or any two of the punishments, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor M. Ramanathan Alias Ashwin proposed bail of RM15,000 with one surety and additional conditions that the accused not interfere with the victim or prosecution witnesses and surrender his passport to the court until the disposal of the case.
Counsel K. Theivaendran, representing the accused, sought a lower bail amount, saying his client was the family breadwinner and also supported his frail 89-year-old mother.
“I object to the prosecution’s application for my client to surrender his passport as he has projects abroad, including in Riyadh (in Saudi Arabia) and is not a flight risk,” he said.
Magistrate Siti Nur Ain Ariffin granted the accused bail of RM9,000 with one surety, imposed the additional conditions sought by the prosecution and fixed Nov 26 for mention.
Media reports last Wednesday said an elderly man had been arrested for allegedly molesting the son of a senior police officer at a gymnasium in Melawati.
The incident is believed to have occurred while the victim was at the gymnasium with a friend. — Bernama

Title: Abang Johari calls for Sarawak state assembly dissolution on Monday
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 23 — The Sarawak State Legislative Assembly is set to be dissolved on Monday, Oct 26, 2026, paving the way for the 13th state election.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg announced the dissolution at a special press conference at the Satria Pertiwi Complex here this afternoon.
He said the decision was made after obtaining the consent of Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar.
“The governor has consented to my request to dissolve the Assembly in accordance with Article 21(2) of the Constitution of the State of Sarawak, with effect from Oct 26.
“Therefore, in accordance with Article 21(4) of the Constitution, the State Election must be held within 60 days from the date of the dissolution,” said Abang Johari.
Abang Johari, who is also Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman, said the Election Commission (EC) will be formally notified of the dissolution to enable the necessary arrangements to be made.
“During this period, the government will discharge its responsibilities in a caretaker capacity, observing the applicable constitutional requirements and conventions.
“Public administration and essential services will continue to ensure that the needs and welfare of the people remain attended to,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says nationwide Waze ban needs careful study first
Article:
AMPANG, Oct 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today proposals for a nationwide ban on navigation app Waze required careful study, but did not rule out the possibility if capable local alternatives were available.
“It must be studied what are the alternatives first, and if we find that local capabilities are good enough then we may consider prohibiting Waze altogether,” he told reporters after performing Friday prayers here.
Anwar again defended the ban on Waze for civil servants amid criticism, describing it as a crucial move to protect national security, even as he acknowledged that the decision had not been deliberated by the Cabinet beforehand.
“This is a heavy issue. When we checked Waze’s headquarters is in Israel, that’s one thing,” he said.
“Then a check showed Waze is governed only by Israeli laws. This is why I had to take a spontaneous decision because we cannot afford to delay even a single day…because all data are automatically handed to the Israeli government.”

Title: Anwar acknowledges complaints about Tuju, urges users to be patient
Article:
AMPANG, Oct 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today acknowledged complaints about local navigation app Tuju but urged users to be patient as its developer works to improve the service, amid the government’s ban on Waze for civil servants.
“If this ban has been bothersome, I apologise. But to me national security is more important,” he told reporters after performing Friday prayers here.
“I feel our own people shouldn’t (criticise Tuju’s developer) harshly. I know the app may have weaknesses but you can always use other apps. Be patient.”
MORE TO COME

Title: Malaysians spend more on eating out than cooking at home as health risks mount, says KRI
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Malaysian households are now spending more on eating out than on groceries to prepare meals at home, according to a new report by the Khazanah Research Institute (KRI).
The report, titled “From Income to Wellbeing: The State of Households 2026”, found that Malaysian households spent an average of RM902.70 a month on eating out, compared with RM875.80 on groceries.
Eating out accounted for 16.2 per cent of total household spending, up from 12.6 per cent in 2016, and was the single biggest driver of higher household expenditure between 2022 and 2024, rising by RM78.20.
According to the report, the increase in food spending was more pronounced among the bottom 80 per cent of households, whose average food expenditure rose by nearly 1.5 times cumulatively between 2019 and 2024.
“For the top 20 per cent (of households), the increase (in food expenditure) was less than 1.3 times,” it said.
The shift in lifestyle has also contributed to concerns over non-communicable diseases, with several Malaysian states recording higher prevalence of diabetes, hypertension and high cholesterol than the national averages in 2023, the report said.
Diabetes was among the top five causes of death in most states between 2022 and 2024, it added.
More than half of Malaysian adults (54.4 per cent) were also above the healthy weight range in 2023, while physical activity declined in urban areas between 2019 and 2023, the report said.

Title: Rafizi instructs lawyers to sue Ramanan, says minister’s graft claims crossed defamation line
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 23 — Former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli has instructed his lawyers to begin defamation proceedings against Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan over corruption allegations the latter made against him yesterday.
In a statement today, Rafizi said he had handed the video and transcript of Ramanan’s press conference to his legal team.
“They believe there are strong grounds to bring a lawsuit against R. Ramanan, as his statements at the press conference crossed the boundaries set by the country’s defamation laws,” he said.
Rafizi said Ramanan, who is also PKR vice-president, had made various allegations against him at the press conference, including accusing him of involvement in corruption.
Rafizi had previously named Ramanan as the PKR MP who allegedly accepted a RM9.5 million bribe to settle a case involving what he described as the “corporate mafia”.
He said yesterday’s press conference confirmed that Ramanan had never filed a lawsuit over that claim, and that the minister had reiterated he would not do so, despite earlier threatening to sue anyone who implicated him.
“If R. Ramanan refuses to sue me, his press conference yesterday has now opened the way for me to take him to court over the allegations he made against me,” Rafizi said.
He added that the legal action was also appropriate as Ramanan continued to evade several corruption allegations concerning him.
Rafizi also said Ramanan’s press conference showed that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s statement in Parliament this week, which claimed Ramanan had initiated court proceedings, was untrue.
He said he would leave it to MPs to take the next step of referring Anwar to Parliament’s Rights and Privileges Committee.

Title: Malaysians remain ‘happy’ as wages recover post Covid-19, but rising costs squeeze poorer households, says KRI
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Malaysians are still classified as “happy” as wages have recovered to above pre-Covid-19 levels, despite household spending rising rapidly among lower-income households, the Khazanah Research Institute (KRI) found in a recent survey.
The report, titled “From Income to Wellbeing: The State of Households 2026”, said median monthly household income reached RM7,017 in 2024, while labour force participation rose to 70.6 per cent that year.
Putrajaya recorded the fastest wage growth, with median monthly household income rising from RM2,700 in 2010 to more than RM4,500 in 2024.
However, the report also noted that nearly half of Malaysian households (46.2 per cent) lived in 22 of the country’s 166 districts, where median monthly household income was below RM7,017.
Some 111 of Malaysia’s 166 districts also recorded poverty rates above the national rate of 5.1 per cent. The poverty rate in 66 districts was more than twice the national rate, the report said.
Even as wages rise, lower-income households are spending more due to rising living costs, leaving them with little disposable income.
The report said household expenditure rose by more than 15 per cent among the bottom 70 per cent of the income distribution between 2019 and 2024.
However, spending barely changed among the top 10 per cent of households.
The squeeze was more severe for the bottom 10 per cent.
“Households in the bottom 10 per cent of the income distribution retained only 1.9 per cent of their gross incomes after covering their consumption expenses, down from 10.8 per cent in 2019,” KRI said in the report.
However, it noted that residual income does not account for tax payments, loan repayments or remittances to other households.

Title: Tighter rules for Malaysian dealers, agents, and accountants? BNM to review money laundering risks next year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) will conduct the next iteration of the National Risk Assessment in 2027, enabling a deeper assessment of the money laundering and terrorism financing risks facing the Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (DNFBP) sectors.
Deputy Governor Datuk Marzunisham Omar said the findings will support the development of more targeted policies, guidance, and mitigation measures tailored to the specific risks faced by each sector.
“Your practical insights will be essential. They will help ensure that our policy responses remain effective, proportionate and grounded in the realities faced by each sector,” he said in his welcoming remarks at DNFBP Compliance Conference 2026, held yesterday.
According to BNM, DNFBP refers to a group that consists of a parent company incorporated in Malaysia or any other type of legal person exercising control and coordinating functions over the rest of the group, together with branches and/or subsidiaries that are subject to anti-money laundering (AML), countering the financing of terrorism (CFT) and countering proliferation financing (CPF) policies and procedures at the group level.
Meanwhile, Marzunisham said the AML, CFT and CPF framework depends not only on strong laws and sound policies, but also on credible supervision and enforcement.
He said the central bank takes non-compliance seriously, as weaknesses in any part of the system could undermine the integrity of Malaysia’s entire AML/CFT framework.
Recent joint enforcement actions involving regulatory and law enforcement agencies reinforce this point.
BNM and the Companies Commission of Malaysia (CCM) recently took enforcement action against a company secretary for failing to submit suspicious transaction reports relating to foreign nationals suspected to be involved in an international scam syndicate.
A Labuan investment bank was subjected to enforcement action by BNM and the Labuan Financial Services Authority (LFSA) following material deficiencies in customer due diligence. This affected the firm’s ability to assess customers’ potential involvement in illicit overseas activities, as well as delays in submitting suspicious transaction reports.
“These cases may involve different sectors and circumstances, but they convey the same message: Weak due diligence, vigilance and reporting create space for criminals to operate.
“Professional services must never become the gate through which illicit funds acquire the appearance of legitimacy, whether knowingly or unknowingly,” Marzunisham added. — Bernama

Title: Holy smoke: Massive ganja and heroin haul found in Klang house of worship
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 23 — Police uncovered drug trafficking at an unregistered house of worship in Klang during operations across Selangor from Oct 13 to 19.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said a local man who worked part-time as an assistant at the house of worship was detained to assist the investigation.
“A raid led to the discovery of 20.6 kilogrammes (kg) of heroin inside the storage room of the house of worship. Investigations are ongoing. We do not rule out that the premises were used to store drugs.
“Checks also revealed that the temple is unregistered and the land is gazetted as a site for sewerage,” he told a press conference at the Selangor Police Contingent Headquarters here today.
In separate raids in Rawang and at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), police arrested seven individuals, comprising two local men, a local woman, three foreign men and a foreign woman, Shazeli said.
He said the individuals, aged between 19 and 48, had no prior criminal records except one local man with seven previous offences.
He added that the operations seized 81.3 kg of cannabis buds, 37 kg of ganja, one bottle and 3,510 cartridges of ketamine, 84 bottles of ecstasy, and 25.4 kg of ketamine.
“The total value of the seized drugs is estimated at RM16.2 million. Police also confiscated two cars, a motorcycle, and local and foreign currencies totalling RM54,835,” he said, adding the case is being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
In a separate case, Shazeli said suspected theft is believed to be the motive behind the abuse of a foreign domestic helper, who suffered burn injuries on her body.
He said investigations found the victim had been working for her employer since late last year.
“Investigations are currently being completed. It is believed the incident occurred because the victim was suspected of stealing and damaging her employer’s property,” he said.
It was reported that three women were among five individuals remanded for four days to assist in the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Borrowers praise PTPTN repayment discounts and deferments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) borrowers have welcomed the repayment relief measures announced under Budget 2027, saying the deferment and lower monthly payments will help ease financial pressures, particularly among fresh graduates.
Under the measures, borrowers earning less than RM2,500 a month will be allowed to defer repayments, while those earning between RM2,500 and RM3,000 will only need to pay a minimum of RM50 a month. Borrowers with no arrears who make regular repayments will also receive a 10 per cent discount.
For Jeremiah Abraham Selvaraj, 43, a cyber security consultant, the education loan was instrumental in helping him complete his bachelor’s degree in mechatronics engineering at Monash University Malaysia and improve his family’s socioeconomic circumstances.
“Without this financial assistance, it would have been impossible for me to complete my higher education. The loan has helped those from lower and middle-income families improve their living standards,” he said.
He described the new repayment measures, including the RM50 monthly minimum, as a considerate move that would help ease the financial burden on fresh graduates.
Jeremiah, who has maintained a consistent repayment record without arrears, also said the 10 per cent discount for regular repayments served as an incentive to maintain financial discipline.
Customer service officer Carol Chan, 24, who is also a PTPTN borrower, welcomed the repayment deferment for those earning less than RM2,500 a month, saying it would give fresh graduates more time to stabilise their finances as they entered the workforce.
“The initiative helps ease our financial burden as we establish ourselves in our careers, allowing us to stabilise our daily expenses and strengthen our finances first,” she said.
Meanwhile, marketing executive Fatin Yusoff, 36, viewed the 10 per cent discount for borrowers without arrears who make regular repayments as recognition of their commitment.
Having maintained her repayments consistently over the past four years, she said the incentive would encourage borrowers to remain disciplined in meeting their obligations.
“When there are incentives like this, it feels as though our efforts are appreciated. The savings from the discount can be channelled into an emergency fund or other essential expenses,” she said.
Hafizul Fiqri Mazlan, 41, a graphic designer at the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (FINAS) who fully repaid his PTPTN loan in 2019, said borrowers should make full use of the repayment incentives.
He said the deferment for borrowers earning less than RM2,500 a month and the RM50 minimum monthly repayment for those earning below RM3,000 would be particularly helpful to those who had just started working.
Hafizul, a former student of Kolej Antarabangsa Yayasan Melaka (KAYM), also welcomed the 10 per cent discount, noting that previously, he had only been able to obtain a discount by settling his loan in full.
He stressed that borrowers had a responsibility to repay their loans so that the funds could continue helping other students pursue higher education.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the repayment measures when tabling Budget 2027 on Oct 9. — Bernama

Title: Police: 19 reports lodged nationwide against man impersonating Selangor Raja Muda’s bodyguard
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 23 — An individual suspected of impersonating the personal bodyguard to the Raja Muda of Selangor to deceive members of the public has been found to have 19 police reports lodged against him nationwide.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said nine of the reports involving the 40-year-old man were lodged in Selangor in connection with fraud cases, with estimated losses totalling nearly RM700,000.
“Police also wish to emphasise that this individual is not a palace staff member and has no links to the Selangor Royal Institution. He is believed to be an ordinary individual who took advantage of his friends by deceiving them,” he said.
He was speaking at a press conference on the achievements of the Selangor Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department at the Selangor police headquarters here today.
Shazeli said police had also detained a woman in her 30s, believed to be the suspect’s fiancée, to assist in the investigation.
He urged members of the public with information to contact the nearest police station or the investigating officer, Sgt Norizuana Saaidin, at 014-7175567. — Bernama

Title: Ministry: PG18 rating signifies age classification, not zero censorship
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The age classification for films rated 18 is not a licence to screen content without restrictions, as such films remain subject to the screening guidelines in force.
The Communications Ministry stressed that the Film Censorship Board (LPF) under the Home Ministry would continue to assess film content based on aspects of public safety and order, religion, sociocultural matters, as well as decency and morality.
"Content that violates the screening guidelines, including material that could undermine social harmony, remains subject to appropriate action,” the ministry said in a written reply published on the Parliament website.
The reply was in response to a question from Datuk Ahmad Saad (PN-Pokok Sena), who asked for the ministry’s position on the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia’s (FINAS) move to stop cutting scenes from films rated PG18 in the name of openness.
The ministry said allowing 18-rated films to be screened without the removal of certain scenes represented a shift from controlling content through scene cuts to regulating access through age-based classification, rather than a relaxation of content restrictions.
It said that under this approach, films meeting the requirements could be screened without certain scenes being cut, but would be subject to strict age classification.
"The 2024 Film Censorship Guidelines detail classification categories based on viewers’ age suitability, which, among other things, enable adults to make informed choices about the films they wish to watch.
"They are also intended to educate and protect teenagers and children from exposure to content that is inappropriate for their age and could affect their behaviour, while placing responsibility on parents to monitor and guide their children in choosing suitable content,” the ministry said.
It added that FINAS and LPF would continue to work with industry players to review the film classification system to ensure it remained relevant to industry developments and the current content landscape.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Media Council (MMM), established following the enforcement of the Malaysian Media Council Act 2025 (Act 868), plays a role in strengthening public media literacy in addressing the spread of false information, hate speech and the challenges posed by digital technology and artificial intelligence (AI).
The Communications Ministry said the council is also responsible for promoting the production of authentic, accurate and ethical media reports and content, strengthening compliance with journalistic codes of ethics, and providing transparent and effective public complaints mechanisms.
"To support the establishment and operation of the MMM, the government has provided legal support through the creation of a dedicated legal framework, as well as initial assistance for infrastructure development and administrative matters.
"Cooperation with relevant agencies also supports capacity-building and the professional development of media practitioners, including through training and the promotion of journalistic ethics,” it said in response to a question from Syahredzan Johan (PH-Bangi) on the implementation status of Act 868 and the MMM, including its functions and responsibilities and the forms of government support provided. — Bernama

Title: MOF: 2pc EPF contribution rate for foreign workers relatively low
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The two per cent Employees Provident Fund (EPF) contribution rate payable by employers for non-Malaysian workers is relatively low, the Finance Ministry (MOF) said.
The ministry said the rate takes into account the need to balance workers’ social protection objectives with the costs borne by employers.
“The government recognises the challenges employers face from rising business costs, particularly small and medium enterprises (SMEs).
“Under the Employees Provident Fund Act 1991, all employers have been required to contribute to the EPF for non-Malaysian workers employed in Malaysia since October 2025,” the ministry said in a written parliamentary reply published on Parliament’s website yesterday.
The ministry was responding to a question from Jimmy Puah Wee Tse (PH-Tebrau) on measures to ease the burden on SMEs amid rising business costs, including whether the government would consider requiring foreign workers to bear the full cost of EPF contributions.
Since mandatory contributions were introduced in October 2025, a total of 78,129 employers have contributed to the EPF for 1,754,460 non-Malaysian workers, the ministry said.
“Of these employers, 86 per cent, or 67,194, were SMEs, defined as businesses with no more than 200 employees in the manufacturing sector and no more than 75 employees in the services and other sectors.
“This indicates that the mandatory contribution requirement has begun to gain acceptance and is being implemented by employers, including SMEs,” it said.
The ministry said mandatory EPF contributions formed part of the government’s efforts to expand social protection coverage to all workers in Malaysia, in line with international practices.
It added that the government remained open to proposals from all parties to improve policies over time.
“The government will continue to monitor the effectiveness of these initiatives and engage with SME associations and communities to ensure that assistance reaches businesses in need,” it said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian banks offer repayment relief to Nepal landslide victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The Association of Banks in Malaysia (ABM) said its member banks are offering repayment deferments and flexible payment arrangements to ease the financial burden on families affected by the landslide in Nepal, including those whose loved ones remain missing.
In a statement yesterday, ABM said the assistance had been available since early October 2026, with member banks reaching out to the affected families.
“We recognise the profound distress and uncertainty faced by the families and next of kin. Their welfare remains our priority, and we appreciate the efforts of all parties working to secure appropriate support for them,” ABM said.
ABM said member banks had designated contact persons to guide affected next of kin, coordinate their requests and help with the necessary documentation and administrative processes.
“ABM and its member banks remain committed to working constructively with Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and all relevant parties to support the affected families with care, compassion and respect,” it said. — Bernama

Title: Abang Johari expected to dissolve Sarawak assembly at 3.30pm today
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 23 — Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg is expected to announce the dissolution of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly this afternoon, paving the way for a state election.
According to a media invitation issued by the Premier’s Office, a special press conference is scheduled for 3.30 pm at the Satria Pertiwi Complex here.
Speculation over the assembly’s dissolution has intensified in recent days amid expectations of an imminent state election.
The assembly held its final sitting of the current term last Wednesday, during which the Sarawak Budget 2027 was passed.
The current term of the 82-seat assembly is due to expire in February 2027.
In the Sarawak state election held on Dec 18, 2021, Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS), led by Abang Johari, secured a landslide victory, winning 76 of the 82 seats contested.
Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) won four seats, while DAP secured two. — Bernama

Title: Lim Guan Eng demands govt reveal cost, tender process and approval behind ‘national embarrassment’ TuJu app
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng today called on the federal government to disclose how much the TuJu road navigation app cost, whether it was awarded through an open tender, and who approved it.
The DAP lawmaker said the app’s failure had become a national embarrassment after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim barred civil servants from using Waze and pointed them to TuJu instead, over sovereignty concerns and the security risk of possible interference by the Israeli government.
TuJu is owned by the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) and was developed by Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd (PCSB).
Lim said the app was launched on November 26, 2025, as a locally developed highway navigation tool, and has been in continuous development for four years since 2022.
“Questions are raised as to how the Prime Minister can be deceived to recommend TuJu when it is defective at best and completely unusable at worst,” he said in a statement.
He claimed that PCSB’s board of directors includes individuals associated with opposition parties. He said there is nothing wrong with opposition politicians securing government contracts, but argued that these directors have no track record or expertise in technology, software engineering or road navigation apps.
“Was there a proper open tender exercise and due diligence carried out as well as who approved a failed TuJu road navigation application?” he asked, adding that the public is still waiting to learn how much was paid to develop the app.
He said the government must come clean in the public interest, to uphold accountability and transparency and “keep the reformist spirit alive”.
The ban on Waze was decided at a National Cyber Security Committee meeting, with Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar instructing department heads to ensure it was implemented immediately.
Anwar said on Tuesday that the government was looking into security risks arising from Waze, which he said was bound by Israeli laws.
The National Cyber Security Agency later clarified that the ban applies only to civil servants on official duty, though it still encouraged them to uninstall Waze and switch to a local alternative.
LLM apologised yesterday for disruptions to TuJu, attributing them to a surge in new users after Anwar’s call, while users also complained about its navigation and route accuracy.
Waze has rejected claims that it collects sensitive government information or allows any party to exploit users’ personal data, calling them false.

Title: HR Ministry: 5,234 Malaysians working abroad have returned via REP since 2011
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — A total of 5,234 Malaysians working abroad have returned to work in Malaysia through the Returning Expert Programme (REP) from 2011 until August this year.
The Ministry of Human Resources (KESUMA), in a written reply in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday, stated that throughout that period, the REP implemented by Talent Corporation Malaysia Berhad (TalentCorp) received 12,850 applications, with 8,093 of them approved.
The programme serves as a mechanism to attract highly skilled Malaysians back to contribute to the national economy.
KESUMA added that to strengthen these efforts, TalentCorp also implements the MyHeart initiative to connect highly skilled Malaysian diaspora with job opportunities matching their experience, expertise, and skill levels.
“As a new component, MyHeart Global Connect (MGC) brings together selected diaspora experts to provide advisory services, share expertise, and explore collaboration opportunities with stakeholders in Malaysia, with an initial focus on artificial intelligence (AI), technology and entrepreneurship, healthcare, and Malaysia-Singapore strategic priorities,” it said.
KESUMA was answering a question from Shaharizukirnain Abd Kadir (PN-Setiu) who wanted to know the effectiveness of the REP based on application statistics, approvals, and the number of experts who have returned to work in Malaysia.
The ministry stated that to facilitate the return of diaspora talent along with their families, the government — through cooperation between KESUMA, the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Malaysian Immigration Department, and TalentCorp — has also provided Entry Permit Application Guidelines under the REP category.
The guidelines aim to provide clearer references regarding the entry permit application procedures for dependents of REP participants, thereby boosting the confidence of highly skilled talent to return to Malaysia with their families.
Meanwhile, for local talent development, KESUMA through TalentCorp implements MyBakat SkillsLab, which as of August 2026 has helped 2,794 participants secure job placements with starting salaries five to 15 per cent higher than the average. — Bernama

Title: Fadhlina: PKR Melaka candidate selection in final stages
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The list of Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) candidates for the Melaka State Election (PRN) is currently being finalised by the party’s top leadership.
PKR Wanita Chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the list has already been submitted for consideration and final decision.
“The decision will be made by PKR’s top leadership to determine our candidates. So, it is currently being finalised,” she said when met after appearing as a guest on Bernama TV’s talk show program Ruang Bicara titled “Budget 2027: Strengthening Education, Shaping the Future” at Wisma Bernama yesterday.
When asked whether the candidates to be featured would comprise of old faces or otherwise, Fadhlina stressed that the party’s priority is to ensure the selected candidates are people-oriented and ready to serve.
“Insya-Allah, what is important are those who are ready to serve the rakyat. Certainly, we want to deliver the best from our party for the people,” she said.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka State Election, with nomination day on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.
The Melaka State Election held in 2021 saw Barisan Nasional (BN) win 21 out of the 28 contested seats, successfully forming the state government, while Pakatan Harapan won five seats and Perikatan Nasional two seats. — Bernama

Title: Indonesian maid in Tanjong Sepat abuse case was accused of theft and damaging property, say Selangor police chief
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 23 — An Indonesian domestic helper was allegedly abused by her employers in Tanjong Sepat, Kuala Langat, after being accused of stealing and damaging their belongings, police said.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the victim is believed to have started working for the suspects around the end of last year or early this year,
Sinar Harian
reported.
“Among the motives for the incident was that the victim was accused of stealing the employer’s belongings and damaging property belonging to the employer. That is their claim,” he was quoted as saying at a press conference at the Selangor police headquarters here today.
Shazeli said the victim’s employers, a married couple, were among those detained to assist investigations.
The abuse is reported to have taken place on October 16, leaving the woman with burns all over her body.
Sinar Harian
had earlier reported that police detained six people, including an employer, at a business premises in Jalan Merbau, Pusat Perniagaan Oren, Butterworth, Penang, at about 6.30pm.
Five of them, including three women, all aged in their 20s and 30s, were remanded for four days from Tuesday until today. The order was issued by Magistrate Maslinda Selamat at the Telok Datok court.
The case is being investigated under Section 12 of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007.

Title: Kuching school attack suspect remains hospitalised as police record 24 statements
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 23 — The 16-year-old male student of an international school here who allegedly attacked a teacher on Wednesday morning is still receiving treatment in hospital, said Sarawak acting police commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak.
“The police are continuing the investigation, taking into account of the suspect’s health condition and subject to the advice and assessment of the medical officers, whilst ensuring that all applicable legal procedures are complied with,” he said in a statement.
Saifullizan said that, as of yesterday, a total of 24 witness statements had been recorded in connection with the investigation.
These included statements from the complainant, the victim, medical officers, officers involved in the arrest and seizure, the suspect’s parents, the family driver, school representatives and students.
“The investigation is being carried out in a professional, thorough and comprehensive manner, taking into account all relevant statements and evidence.
“Any further action will be taken based on the facts obtained and the provisions of the law in force.
“The police also take seriously the need to be sensitive towards all parties, in particular the welfare of the victim and the students involved.
“The public is requested to respect their privacy and not to disseminate identities, photographs or personal information that could lead to the identification of any party, especially minors,” he said.
The police received a report on the alleged attack at around 8.03am via the MERS 999 emergency line.
The teacher reportedly sustained injuries to her hand during the incident.
The alleged attack has raised concern in Kuching after it was live-streamed and went viral on social media. Saifullizan confirmed the circulation of the video in a report by Sinar Harian.
The circulation of videos and photographs has drawn various reactions from netizens, with many condemning the alleged attack while others expressed shock and concern over safety in schools.
Some social media users voiced fears about the possibility of such violence occurring in a school environment, while others expressed sympathy for the teacher and those who witnessed the incident.
The live-streamed video has since been taken down by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC). — The Borneo Post

Title: Zahid: BN and PAS to announce Melaka candidates tomorrow
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 23 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will announce its candidates for the Melaka State Election, with PAS and its strategic partners, tomorrow, said its chairman, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, said BN will contest 21 seats, while PAS and its strategic partners will contest seven seats, based on the seat allocation agreed upon thus far.
“God willing, on the same stage and in the same hall, we will make the announcement (regarding the candidates for BN, PAS, and the strategic partners),” he told reporters after chairing a meeting of BN Supreme Council at Melaka International Trade Centre here last night.
Regarding the distribution of seats among BN component parties, Ahmad Zahid noted that the matter has been finalised based on the projected winnability of each party in the respective constituencies.
He added that PAS and its strategic partners have also held meetings to discuss the allocation of seats among themselves.
“God willing, everything will be resolved smoothly... everything has been finalised in accordance with the number of seats we have mutually agreed upon,” he said.
In a related development, Ahmad Zahid announced that the Chief Minister, who also serves as the Melaka BN chairman, Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, has been appointed as the BN election director for this state election.
He explained that Ab Rauf has taken over the role from Umno deputy president and Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, who has overseas commitments during the campaign period.
“As it happened, during the campaign period in Melaka, he (Mohamad) had numerous overseas commitments including attending Commonwealth meetings, representing the country at regional gatherings, participating in the Asean Summit, and visiting several other nations,” he said.
The Election Commission has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with nomination day on October 31 and early voting on November 10.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, BN won 21 out of the 28 contested State Legislative Assembly (DUN) seats, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured five seats and Perikatan Nasional (PN) won two. — Bernama

Title: ECRL Gombak station’s covered link bridge to LRT ready by March 2027, temporary walkway in place for December launch
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Passengers using the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) Gombak station will have a temporary walkway to the Gombak LRT station when services begin in December, while a permanent covered pedestrian bridge linking the two is set for completion by March 2027, Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) said today.
In a statement this morning, MRL said the bridge will also extend to the Gombak Integrated Terminal (TBG), while the temporary walkway will run through existing connecting areas and Prasarana facilities.
It said the temporary route will take into account passengers’ safety, comfort and ease of movement, including for those carrying luggage.
It added that it is also in talks with Prasarana on a proposed shuttle service between the two stations as an additional option, particularly for passengers with luggage.
MRL was responding to public concerns over passenger movement between the ECRL Gombak station, the Gombak LRT station and TBG.
It stressed that pedestrian access and public transport integration at the station had been factored into the ECRL project’s development plans from the outset.
The company said providing pedestrian access is part of its effort to ensure the ECRL Gombak station functions as a public transport hub integrated with the existing rail and transport network.
It also gave an assurance that temporary access is being arranged to meet passenger needs when services open, while the permanent bridge is completed in stages.
